utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D28.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will the usher please show the witness the second photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I might take this opportunity as well to state that the Prosecution will be seeking in due course as well to rely on certain video evidence. And I hope that Mr. Petrovic will be as forthcoming in agreeing to the submission of such videos, photographs, et cetera, without raising any matters with respect to the admissibility of such evidence at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're hoping for some reciprocal understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Indeed. Your Honour, I think it would be beneficial to both sides and to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber would certainly encourage discussion between Prosecution and Defence to remove any difficulties over such things, because it is of significance if we can avoid unnecessary wasting of time over technical issues. If the parties can reach agreement over the nature of the exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we shall exhibit the maximum of cooperativeness. Of course, once we know exactly what is in question, which I'm sure my learned colleague will appreciate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me what is on the left side of the photograph in front of you. Is this the Minceta fortress?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say it's the Minceta fortress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this green part that you see behind, is that the Bogisicev Park, do you know that it is in that direction, the park that is immediately next to the Old City?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's Bogisicev Park, which is behind the Imperial Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your statement, sir, that you would be surprised if the Croats were operating so close to the Old Town from Bogisicev Park. Now, why would that be a surprise to you?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the surprise is that they would have anything -- well, one of the surprises is that if this was operating near the park, I'm surprised that nobody said anything about that. That's one thing. I don't know if it's 200 metres from the old walls of the town; I thought it was a bit further than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is cause also, your concern?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere it does cause some concern. It does cause some concern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what would cause your concern, if they were operating from this park, which was so close to the Minceta fortress?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, my answer is based also on my experience, my experience in Croatia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina, especially after this period. I'm not -- I didn't know that this position was there when I was on mission. So if I was -- I'm not entirely sure what I would have thought. But afterwards on the basis of experience that I had in the war zones, I would be concerned that something 4 or 500 metres away from a location which I would hope and expect to be protected, I would be concerned that the proximity, even if 4 or 500 metres, would be used as a pretext to shoot at the object I was concerned about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this would worry you because this would directly endanger a protected property?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that it could be used as a pretext to endanger property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you really expect the Croats to tell you that their mortar position was several hundred metres away from the Old Town? Did they really expect them to admit this to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Once again I think that is speculative, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that this is a question which is wholly in place. I am in your hands. I believe that the witness can reply to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you would. If you had an expectation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know exactly when this mortar position was operating. The -- I don't think the investigator indicated a date. The picture you showed me has a date of 4th of November on it. I don't know if it was there. I mean, maybe it was there before and it was moved. Maybe it was not moved. If any authorities could speculate on what might be the consequences, justified or not, of having a mortar position 4 or 500 metres from the walls, I think that they should be concerned about it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kaiser, during the break the Prosecution gave me the statement of a witness - whose name I shall refrain from mentioning right now; the colleagues, of course, know who is in question - which mentions that it was also precisely on the 6th of December that fire was opened from exactly the same position that I'm talking to -- about right now. This witness who will be appearing before this Chamber. Are you still surprised?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me if I'm surprised now. I am still surprised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a rich experience in the countries of the former Yugoslavia in these unfortunate times. Was it rare for someone to do a thing like that, namely to position a military target immediately upon a protected piece of property? How often had you had occasion to see something of the kind? Was this something that happened only seldom in the wars which took place in the former Yugoslavia in this period, or was this an element of the daily tactics of the warring factions, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a considerable problem I think in urban areas which could have cultural heritage nearby, might not have cultural heritage nearby. And there are unfortunately a number of substantiated examples of ordnance being used inside towns. That I'm pretty sure about. It's a little harder to say in rural areas or beside towns. But it is true, it is definitely true, that ordnance was used from places where it really should not have been used. If people were thinking about -- supposed to be thinking about the security of their civilian population, thinking about that first, and possibly also valuable buildings, valuable historically speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times during your time in the former Yugoslavia did you see a church, a mosque, or a monument of culture being used for firing from? Was this often the case? I'm not asking you about the specific number of times that you saw that.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to avoid shooting zones as much as possible, so my observation of these matters I didn't really observe them. The problem was that when you observed damage you weren't sure -- I mean, the -- it was often alleged that a church tower or even a minaret was being used as a firing position or a military observation point. It was very hard to demonstrate that this, in fact, had been the case. If you found -- if you found spent cartridge cases in a church tower, then you could be pretty well sure that it was so. And I've even heard of examples where minarets were supposedly -- eyewitnesses actually used. These are very, very hard things to determine, especially after the fact; I fear that they were, though, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on and look at your statement in connection with this story about how many people were in uniform and how many people were without uniform. You say in your statement: "There were many people walking around with personal weapons," and further, "there were very few people in military or police uniform. Of those people in uniform that I did see, those were in what I believed to be military uniform. In the Old Town there were no Croatian units or equipment positioned." Is it correct that the ratio between those in uniform and those with weapons was in favour of those who were carrying weapons but did not wear uniform and that you saw a great number of those, as stated in your statement?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing I'd like to say is when we first came to Dubrovnik we went to visit Stefan Dimistura. Stefan Dimistura was the head of the mission in Dubrovnik, and he is a very well-known international functionary, a very, very respected one. Dimistura told us that there were -- I can't remember if he said many, but he said there were certainly people not in uniform in the town with weapons. Now, on one occasion I did see somebody take out a hand gun. On other occasions I just looked at people, and this is something I saw off and on all through the war is that people would always put their hand guns in the back of their belt. And so there would be a bulge, often a bulge at the back. And if you looked around and you could see somebody with a bulge, you say, Well, he may have a hand gun back there. And to say many, it's -- I didn't count them. There were definitely people in the town not in uniform who had had hand guns. It is true. But to say what the ratio was between soldiers and people with hand guns in civilian uniform, really, sir, I couldn't say -- give any idea about the ratio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would please ask you to provide brief answers, if you can, sir, because we don't have too much time to waste. Sir, is it true what it says here that many people were walking around? Is that true or not? Do you stand by your statement where you said that many people were walking about town?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people, sir. I wouldn't say many. There were certainly some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why did you say "many" in your statement to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a civilian with a rifle?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see any civilians, or people in civilian dress with long-barrelled weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any civilians with a mortar perhaps?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for the one that I showed you in that photograph from the Bogisicev Park?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for the one in your photograph, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, tell me, please, what is HOS?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, HOS was a right-wing Croatian militia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a paramilitary unit?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a paramilitary unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does "right" mean? Right as in radical nationalists? What's so right-wing about them?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, radical nationalists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any members of the HOS in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a couple of individuals who were wearing some sort of patch. They were also pointed out to me as being members of HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the difference between members of the HOS and Croatian regular forces?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I could make any difference out, except on the basis of the insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inform Nikola Obuljen about the fact that paramilitary troops were walking about town?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't inform -- we didn't inform him about that. At least I didn't inform Bruno Carnez about that. But I don't know, I don't think that we informed him about that, and there were one or two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the presence of paramilitary units worry you?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know what HOS was up to or what HOS was. But I think I mentioned in my earlier statement that one of the UNICEF internationals had trouble with one of these guys and was sort of -- sort of saved by the people of Dubrovnik who informed the HOS member that this man had come with UNICEF to help the people of Dubrovnik, that it was not an enemy of the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This HOS member who attacked the UNICEF official, was this man arrested? Were his weapons taken from him?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, because I there. I don't know what happened after this encounter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the Croatian army was facing difficulty with members of the HOS in the town at the time?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know this. I knew on other occasions the Croatian army, or Croatian troops in Bosnia were having trouble with them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know about conflicts breaking out between the Croatian regular forces and members of the HOS inside the town?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't know about any such conflicts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you if the regular Croatian forces made an attempt to disarm those paramilitary units and that a clash could have broken out?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now it wouldn't surprise me. At the time I didn't know what these different units were; I didn't know what their relations were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any of the members of the HOS were ever prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you afraid yourself -- were you afraid -- were you concerned about your own security when you heard that HOS members were attacking international officials who were present in town?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't afraid because the -- as I mentioned before, there were only a couple of them we saw in the town. They didn't seem to have much of a presence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But still they did manage to attack an international official, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. And he was protected by the people of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know those HOS members had taken part in military operations against the federal forces?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what operations they had taken part in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to ask you now something about your own perception of events of the 6th of December. Is it correct that you had an impression, as you said in your statement, the sounds you heard that morning were coming from nearby? I'm talking about the morning of the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned, the first impression I had of the sounds when I woke up is that the sounds were really up on the hill towards Srdj or in that area. They weren't so close. There were a lot of them, but they didn't seem to be so close. And then later on the sounds all of a sudden moved down quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you said the following: "It seemed to me that I could distinguish between three different types of sound and they were all coming from nearby." If you can - I know this may not be too easy to put into words - but can you please try to describe these three respective types of sound to me.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not -- well, the sound that I remember really very distinctively because it was repetitive in the early part of the bombardment was -- there was a series of whams, very metallic sounds like something striking stone and these sounds were at intervals. You could count between the explosions. This is one of the sounds. There was another sound that was kind of a whistle, not a -- kind of a hiss, whistle, which seemed to be a lower sound. Projectiles coming in close to the roofs. There were big booms, which I assumed to be the mortar -- mortar sound -- the mortars coming in. And then there was a few other sounds which were louder, sort of -- this was -- this was I think the one that I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, can you distinguish between an explosion, a detonation, from the sound of an artillery weapon firing? Can you distinguish between those two? If so -- or rather, were you able to distinguish at the time, back then, and why?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking if I can -- if one can distinguish between the sounds of different projectiles, and my answer to that is yes. I don't think back then I could distinguish perhaps as well as I could distinguish later on. I would definitely say that the big booms were mortars, but I was not -- I'm not an expert now and even my experience later didn't make me an expert. But I could tell some noises a lot better and what they were later on. But a few sounds on this day sort of did stand out and they were different projectiles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know about is the part where you say - if it's been interpreted correctly - that you heard them daily. Was that your first experience ever of that kind, the morning of the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I heard them daily? I heard these sounds daily? I don't understand. What did you ask me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may have been a misinterpretation. I don't believe you said you heard those sounds daily. But at any rate, was this your first experience of the kind, in your life I'm saying, the morning of the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that morning could you distinguish between an explosion and the sound of an artillery weapon being fired? Could you distinguish the explosions of shells on the one hand and the sounds of artillery weapons firing on the other? Or were all these sounds sounds that just merged for you and you could not distinguish?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I could distinguish between the piece being fired and the detonation coming -- when it hit. I could distinguish between different types of detonations and some coming, but I could not honestly differentiate between the moment of firing and when it hit, an explosion, that it made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you spent the best part of that day, or rather the entire day practically and the night, first at the institute and then in the monastery where you had taken shelter, or you tried to sleep in the basement?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we spent most of the day in the Dominican Monastery. And then, of course -- and then the night after the bombardment as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were not able to see anything that was going on outside? For example, if there were any soldiers in the Old Town or artillery weapons or anything like that for that matter because you spent the entire day between 5.48 in the morning and nightfall shut up. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were out briefly, and that was simply when we went from the institute to the Dominican Monastery. But what you're saying is essentially correct; I was shut up so I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question by my learned friend and colleague on 8th and 9th of February this year, you said that at the beginning there were 82-millimetre shells and then 120-millimetre shells came, followed by marker shells, and so on and so forth. How was it that you were able to distinguish from the basement of the monastery that 82-millimetre shells were falling or marker shells? How were you able to know that? This was your first experience of shelling, as you said; and secondly, there was not a thing that you could actually see from the basement, where you were?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a question of this so-called rocket, and we had been carrying out the survey of the damage of October and November and looking to see where this particular projectile landed, how it landed. We saw that there would be a group of them, sometimes in a line, but sometimes not. There would be a group of them. This particular projectile I assumed when it was fired it could be fired in sequence. And so these various whams that I mentioned -- and the Dominican Monastery was actually hit by this projectile. We could see a few things out the window, by the way. I assumed that this particular projectile, that noise, was coming in fact from that rocket. You're right, I couldn't see what the other things were and when they were coming in. We're talking mainly on the basis of what was picked up after the bombardment. Of course I was in --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe my question is very specific. How can someone who holds a Ph.D. who is in a basement taking shelter from the shelling that is going on outside, how would such a person facing such a situation for the first time in his life be able to distinguish between the various types of shell? I think the only logical answer that I can see is that you are not able to distinguish.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not an expert. I mean, I heard different kinds of noises and they didn't seem to be too many different kinds of noises. And there weren't too many different kinds of shells picked up. You're right, I couldn't tell if it was a Marching 1 that was being fired. I don't think that the -- this particular rocket -- I was not wrong about the noise that it made when it hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mortar rockets you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we called it a rocket. And I have later seen it described, in fact, as a mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it that you realised that this was called mortar? That was just after the 6th of December; right?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was later on that I came across -- I believe it was one of the documents in UNESCO. In the UNESCO action plan, it indicates this in fact as a mortar. This is the one with the wings that we called a rocket. But it is a brand of mortar that has a flat trajectory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to your report later and we'll go into great detail when examining your report. But what I want to know is when exactly you realised this, because your report was published in October 1993, which means two years later. And your report still states "rocket." So when was it that you realised specifically that those were no rockets, in fact, but rather mortars. I can locate the exact spot in your report, if you like. When then, if it wasn't on the 7th or 8th or 9th of December, how come you know this very well now, 12 years later, but you didn't know it back in 1993 or didn't seem to?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my report wasn't published in 1993. I think it was perhaps included as a document in the report of the commission of experts. It was never published. It was not -- if it had been published, then perhaps there would have been a correction, a correction made of it. But it was not published. There was no particular need for it to be corrected; it went to the director-general and the culture sector. It wasn't supposed to go any further than that. So I don't understand -- in 1992 UNESCO was working on an action plan, and I remember seeing this particular -- it's a page in the beginning of the action plan, and it gives the different types of projectiles. It was shown the other day, and this -- I noticed that it was a mortar written on it. So I assumed that it was a mortar and not a rocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you referred in your report to the fact that those were not rockets but rather mortars. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in my report it's mentioned as a rocket all the time, I believe, incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did you make the correction for the first time, when you came here to testify or earlier?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was pointed out to me that I was making mistakes in the shells, and in fact it really was a mortar. But then there was no reason for me to correct my report. Now, keep in mind there's also two mortars. There's two 82-millimetre mortars. One of them is the flat trajectory mortar with the little fins, the little wings on it, and the other 82-millimetre mortar is a little squat -- little squat thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What else do you want to know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you clarify about the flat trajectory mortar. What exactly is it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Well, the flat trajectory mortar shell which we called -- we called that the rocket. And that was in -- we found in the very tops of buildings and it was always on the very same side usually of the buildings. And that was what we called the rocket. This is the one that pierces -- it pierces the stone. We had been informed that this particular projectile -- and we saw inside of it, it had an explosive charge at the front of it and it had a little metal cylinder. And when the charge exploded, this little metal cylinder came out and this sort of projectile was used normally for vehicles to pierce armour. This is the difference between that one and the ordinary little squat mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the trajectory of the other projectile, the other mortar that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other one is a higher trajectory, so you don't find it on walls. You find it coming on to roofs, it comes into flat, stone surfaces on the Stradun and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you about marking mortars, what they were? How did you learn about that? What is it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a marking mortar is used -- it makes a lot of smoke when it explodes, therefore it marks a position. And if you have visual sighting on a target, then you can send the mortars in. If you want to hit this particular area, you sight your weapon on the smoke that's coming up. So it's used for marking targets. It's used apparently as a -- eventually as a smoke screen. Who told us about this? This -- I cannot remember exactly who told us in Dubrovnik and when they told us about this particular weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you said that the shelling was the heaviest during the initial hours. Is that correct? And then you say: "It died down later on," when you heard individual shots coming probably from the ships. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true -- it is true that the heaviest part of the shelling was at the beginning for a few hours. And the shelling then became more selective and less intensive as time went on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you heard firing from the ships. Right?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a problem. This is a discussion. At the time when we were listening to the shelling, Mr. Carnez felt that there was a certain regular pattern of firing. And Mr. Carnez in fact is a former paratrooper, and it was true that there seemed to be some sort of regular firing pattern. After -- excuse me for being very long-winded, sir --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could just try to be brief, because there are so many things for us to go through. I will be glad to give up some of my questions to speed things along a little bit in return. But sorry for interrupting you, sir.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, the whole question about the boats is for me up in suspension marks. I don't know if there really were boats. At the time of the writing of the report it still seemed that there were boats because it was odd impacts on the inside of the city walls that could not identify as being likely from the usual types of ordnance. Therefore, they might come from ordnance shot from a boat, but later on those impacts were identified as, in fact, coming from the usual types of ordnance. Therefore, the question of the boats is I don't know anything about it. I am rather dubious about the boats -- at least shooting on the Old Town. If there were boats, maybe they were shooting at something else. But I am dubious about the boats and the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At which point in time did that become unimportant? You gave your statement two years ago and you stated clearly "from ships." How come it strikes you as so unimportant now? What has happened in the meantime to make it seem so unimportant all of a sudden? Have you perhaps remembered something? Have you talked to someone else? It's been ten years, after all.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It just sort of gets weaker and weaker, this idea. Also, you know, is it the fact that -- as I mentioned, that there were not strange projectiles identified in the damage assessment done by the institute. I just don't believe it anymore. I can't tell you when I gave this idea up, but I was dubious about this idea in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So since the year 2000 this idea grew vaguer and weaker. How -- you were discussing this with someone and then you were sort of gradually relinquishing this idea or perhaps you were examining your own impressions? How is it that the idea got weaker and weaker. I find this really difficult to understand. Maybe it's up to me; maybe it's my fault. But I find it's very hard to understand.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given my answer on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say: "As time went by, the shooting died down and sounded more selective as though someone was trying to target -- someone was searching for something." Can you please explain that phrase, "someone was searching for something," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to go back to the boats again, but this was about -- this is a question of, sort of, intervals of shooting. And that -- and those intervals seemed to imply that -- it's an intuition, that statement. There was intervals, and it seemed to me that something -- that people were aiming at something specifically. I may have been wrong; I was sitting in the Dominican Monastery, but I noticed this sort of interval shooting going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had the impression that someone was trying to target very specific targets. Correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that on that day the blaze in the houses that were on fire was getting stronger and stronger on account of a strong wind?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- I think the buildings functioned as a bit as a chimney and if there is a wind blowing very strongly, it would get worse. The fear was, and I went out in the evening, was that we knew the wind was blowing and the fear was that in fact the fires would spread.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the wind was very strong that day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It rose steadily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us something about the methods, the working methods, you used when assessing the damage in the town of Dubrovnik. Would you agree with my assessment that the method applied was one of total improvisation as to the assessment of the precise time and of the way the damage had come about?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Total improvisation is the assessment of the exact time and way. You're talking about 6th of December, following the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the question was -- there was damage which was done earlier. October the 23rd, the 10th to the 12th of November, that damage had been identified. Any other damage which there would be would be done on the 6th of December. There is no idea when -- what time the damage was done on the 6th of December. I don't think that's -- it's not so totally improvised and it's not totally off. The second part of your question is the way the damage come about. I would say that we had hoped and we had instructed and we had explained to the members of the institute something about the type of damage done by different projectiles that we had been able to observe in the earlier bombardments. Now, we're not -- I'm not a specialist of ballistics, however we thought we had good -- can I continue? I want to explain --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, please.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question of whether or not I remember the institute got every shell right is something that can indeed be asked. I've been over a few of the sheets, and we see light damage done by 120-millimetre mortar. Well, I'm not sure it's light damage and the roof is scratched by a direct hit by a 120-millimetre mortar. Then we see heavy damage on the roof done by an 82-millimetre mortar. I don't think so. So, there will be some discrepancies. These people were not experts in ballistics either. If they could get the -- pick up the shell in the vicinity, in the close vicinity, of the damage, then that was the best way to know what damage it did. I will stop there. I hope I've answered your questions, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you have. But I'm afraid we'll need to go back to that for further detail once we get to your report. Tell me, sir: What is your experience in assessing damage in this way? Just briefly, one sentence, if you can. Is it extensive? Do you have any experience at all?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One word, sir: None.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your general experience in assessing the state of conservation of a building, for example? Have ever done that? Have you carried out assessments of architectural features of a building and its state of preservation?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I'm not a special -- I'm not an architect. And I'm not an art historian either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So even in that area your experience is as good as nonexistent?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a way to say it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that you were trying to focus on damage that had been caused to the buildings; that was your primary interest, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were several interests. One of the interests was damage, if war damage had been done. The other question was to make some recommendations as to what should be restored, what were the priorities of restorations. I knew the different types of buildings and the value of the individual buildings. So there were two things, not just damage, also questions of priorities for restoration and recommendations for restoration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have referred to Mr. Zvonko Franic on various occasions and to the Vetma family. Did they have any previous experience in assessing damage to buildings, architectural, in terms of construction?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were members of the institute for the protection of cultural heritage; they were architects. It was their job to assess damage, to assess the value of buildings; and this was something they had done as part of their job before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So their daily work was to assess the state of preservation of a building, to assess the damage, whereas Dubrovnik was your first encounter with that type of work?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you did these assessments, did you also ascertain the direction of the projectile in question, from which direction the projectile which damaged the building in question came? Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with -- dealing with the 82-millimetre mortar, it was usually - rocket mortar - it was usually easy to find out which direction it came from. On the other hand, dealing with the little 82-millimetre mortar, dealing with the 120-millimetre mortar, it was much more difficult and most of the time you couldn't really tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to ascertain from which particular direction a mortar shell, an 82-millimetre shell, was fired? What were the characteristics that you observed so that you were able to tell it was fired from this or that particular position?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you heard on Friday, there were certain -- there was a number -- a good number of 82-millimetre mortar rockets which were actually stuck in walls. So you could tell where they came from. There were others -- if they were not stuck in the wall, they had made damage to the wall. They had left a particularly narrow impression -- a narrow cylindrical hole, some of the pieces had gone through the wall, as we encountered for the earlier type of damage. And if you would drew a straight line backward, you would see it was coming from -- these particular shells were coming from the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does there exist a mortar which has a straight-line trajectory of the shell which it fires? And is this the 82-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the flat trajectory of the 82-millimetre mortar, the little wings on the end, the cylinder mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So an 82-millimetre mortar shell at each site or most of the sites that you observed, that you examined, you were able to ascertain for each of these shells from which direction it had come?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most of the time, for this particular shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you put that down in your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look in the annex 3, you will see where the damage is meant -- what walls the damages are found on. And it's in the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this a convenient time, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm in your hands. I'm slightly carried away with my questioning. Of course. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you'll be able to collect your thoughts during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It is not a question of collecting my thought; it of is the voluminousity [as interpreted], the bulk, the sheer bulk of the questions that I wish to address in posing questions to this particular witness. Thank you, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We noticed, Mr. Petrovic. We will have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaiser, before the break we spoke about these shells, projectiles, and the trajectories of them. And you said that in your report marked as P61 in tabulater [as interpreted] 6 that you also indicated the directions from which the shells were coming. So, sir, please tell me: Was this the procedure that you also used in the preliminary report for the Institute for the Protection of Heritage, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were talking about these particular shells. I explained to you how I came about indicating where they came from. The preliminary report institute report you're talking about is the one done after the bombardment of the 6th of December or the one before, the preliminary report?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to this report, I didn't instruct people to speculate about where the shells were coming from. This was not really part of it. It was really looking at the type of damage. It was not strongly underlined by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was your primary concern. Were you also interested in the type of ammunition which inflicted the damage?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or was the time also of the infliction of damage important in the preliminary report you prepared for the institute?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By timing we're talking about the dates; we're not talking about any specific times in the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the days. Not the time of day during that period but the actual days.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the date was important. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a police investigation undertaken to ascertain the damage levels in the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if a police investigation was undertaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any crime or ballistics technician or expert on your team?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever prepare a report quantifying the damage that was sustained?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "quantifying"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean the number of buildings that were damaged and the equivalent of the damage in terms of money.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the preliminary report of the institute was to determine the number of buildings that were damaged, the type of damage that it was. We -- we were asked by headquarters in the days following the bombardment to get together some figures. I mean, this was a very unrealistic kind of exercise. And we got together some figures, but they were not very useful figures finally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement at a certain point you refer to -- you say: "We agreed for the needs of the investigators to prepare this preliminary report for the investigators." Do you remember this particular part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You're saying that I said we were preparing the report for investigators of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Not the ICTY. Generally for the requirements of investigators. The ICTY did not exist at the time. For the needs of the investigation. I can read the entire paragraph. "On this day, we -- that day we gathered with members of the institute, Bruno and I knew we had to act quickly. We agreed on a pro forma standard report for the investigators to use, to list the date of the damage," and so on. "We were most interested in mapping the damage." Was this correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These investigators, the people who were going to be doing the survey. It's not police investigators or Tribunal investigators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are the investigators for the needs of whom you undertook to make this preliminary report? This is what I failed to understand?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We agreed on a pro forma report for the investigators to use. To list the damage, et cetera, et cetera. These were the members of the institute and the volunteer architects. Was"investigator" used in the English, or was it a translation? But these are not -- these are the people who were carrying out the damage survey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Have you read the preliminary report, which is marked P51 here? Have you ever read it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never read it through in its entirety. I saw -- you remember that my assignment was finished at the end of December. I wrote my report. That was ongoing work. It was sent in a Serbo-Croatian version, and I was much less conversant in Serbo-Croatian, even than I am today. The bits -- I saw bits of it. When the investigator Stephens came along and showed me what I had done myself. And then I saw it, sort of, when I came here for the appearance in the Tribunal. I saw an English version of it. I have never read the report in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this report before it was published or had you already left Dubrovnik by that time?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were working on it in Dubrovnik when we left. I didn't know it was -- I didn't know it was published.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have an occasion to inspect the content of the report at that time? At the time of its publication, that is.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have an opportunity to investigate -- to study this report in 1992 when it came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the report consists of individual minutes or records that were made related to the individual buildings and structures?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's exactly what it consists of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- did you also personally undertake this inspection in a number of cases?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a number of cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you show the record that you compiled to anyone?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forms that we worked on and I was working with Mr. Franic, those forms were simply given in to the institute when they were finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which way did you participate in the shaping of this form for the inspected buildings when these reports were made solely and exclusively in the Croatian language, which you do not speak?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the form that you see was a form that I had designed and it was for the earlier bombardments. So that was a methodological contribution to the report. I remember addressing the institute as the beginning -- at the beginning of the survey, just going through the different points and explaining to them what we were looking for, what we were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please stick to the subject. I'm asking you whether you read what was written in the form, for the concrete buildings that you undertook to inspect. Did you read it? I believe that I'm quite clear. I can quote for you what I'm referring to. Book number 1, Z24 to 25, book 35 to 36, and book seven zones, Z28 to 12. Did you read these, because your signature is underneath -- under it. Did you read these?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I misunderstood you. Yes, I read these when they were handed in, to agree that that was in fact what was in fact, you know, what was in them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking. How did you read them, seeing that they were in the Croatian language?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I didn't read them afterwards. I read them at the moment they were put in as a contribution to the work of the institute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read the specific documents contained in the preliminary reports, under which is your signature? The final product, did you read the final product? Have you ever seen the final product?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The final product in Serbo-Croatian was shown to me, but -- I mean, it was shown to me in 2001. And -- I mean those surveys were carried out years before. And as I said to you, I'm not at all a proficient Serbo-Croatian reader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the year 2001 you can practically not remember any of the specific damage to the specific buildings in the report forms that you signed. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you examine the records that were drawn up by other people?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked through an English edition of it. There's an English translation of this, and I just -- I flipped through and I looked at a number of the entries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, can we clarify this particular question. I'm asking about the years 1991, 1992, and 1993. I'm not asking you about the year 2001. I'm referring to the translation which was made by the Prosecution of the ICTY. Did you ever -- when the report was being prepared, did you study? Did you look at what other people were preparing for the report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were doing the surveys, I can remember discussing with the teams on a few occasions. I cannot remember reading these different forms which were done -- by and large produced when I was no longer there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you prepared to shoulder the responsibility for the accuracy of what is written by other people in these forms? Do you assume that as yours, as your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's some responsibility for setting up the methodology and launching this exercise. As I was never engaged by UNESCO to go back and look at that report and compare it with the reality, I cannot assume total -- I cannot assume responsibility for something that was completely out of my hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the preparation of the preliminary report thus was not under your control and you did not influence the shaping of the final -- of the end product, the final report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very beginning stages were under our control, but you're perfectly right about -- in most of your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So am I right when I say that apart from designing the methodology, that you had no other influence on the preliminary report, am I not?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from what influence we may have had in discussions with the teams while we were still in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you neither saw the final report nor did you sign it nor were you able to read it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this preliminary report, was there ever a final report prepared on the damage which was inflicted?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't believe that there was because the institute found itself drawn immediately into the UNESCO -- the preparation of the UNESCO plan for restoration of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your reports -- just bear with me for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. Can the witness please be shown this Exhibit Number 61, tabulater 6 -- 62, my apologies. I think the number is 62. [In English] Sir, I think it is 62. P62. [Interpretation] The report by Mr. Kaiser, the two-volume report that we had the last time. Tab 6, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At tab 6, can you see your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at annex 3 to your report. Is this the annex to your report, so not to the institute's report, to your report, the annex describing the damage inflicted in October and November 1991. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that you compiled this report with accuracy and conscientiously, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown two other exhibits marked for identification as P51. Those are two binders. Can these two please be given to the witness; he'll need them to compare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, sir -- first of all, I will ask you to look at annex 3 of your report, and look at -- this appears to be in French. Unfortunately I'm not conversant in French but I will try to find my way around, as we don't seem to have an English translation of annex 3. I hope, however, that this will not prove to be an insurmountable problem for all of us. On page 1 of annex 3, please -- first of all, please tell me, at the top of the page it says that this refers to the damage inflicted in October and November 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there's a list under A with buildings that you inspected and ascertained damage that was sustained in October and November 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first listed building, the building listed as damaged at some date in October, November is the Drezvenik fort, is it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you please look at -- in binder 1, P51, can you please look at Z12, Z13, and Z14.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will try to be of assistance to you also. In the English version of P51, these are the pages that are marked as L0061344, 345, and 346.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaiser, that's in the upper left corner of the page, 434, 435, and 436. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now show me these qualifications, Z12, 13, and 14, do these refer to the Drezvenik fort and the adjacent portion of the wall?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These refer to section of the wall near to -- it was Drezvenik Bastion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that correspond with what you wrote in your report? Is it the same building we are talking about, the same building from your report. If you could please read the French. I really don't read French. I'm not sure what there is under 1, direct impact by a 82-millimetre shell. I believe it states that it hit the wall just next to the bastion. I really can't say what it says in French. Please, can you look at A1.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see is that it hit the platform on the bastion itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, do we seem to have a problem there? Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have not located the documents to which you are referring yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies. Your Honours, the English translation, the pages as I have indicated in binder 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Could you please give us a number in English again. That number doesn't seem to be in my binder at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, here it goes: L0061434, L0061435, L0061436. That's the number in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. We've now -- two out of three have succeeded. Three out of three can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, again my apologies. I believe you will soon realise why I am trying to show this to the witness. My apologies again. I know this is inconvenient, but I would like the witness to first of all look at annex 3 from his own report and read what it says precisely under A1 Drezvenik Bastion, direct impact by 82-millimetre shell, and that's as far as I can stretch my knowledge of French. If the witness can please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Direct impact of 82-millimetre rocket on the pavement and fragments on the west wall of the platform. This is on the bastion. Platform of the bastion. West wall of the platform of the bastion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaiser, can you please find this same piece of damage in P51, if you can. Are there any references to it? The document that comprises October, November, and December. In my view it would be Z12, 13, and 14, because that refers to the same thing. If that's it, then okay. If not, please find what is it.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the locations, the locations are walkways basically between the towers. There's no reference to the actual hit on the tower. The first one says city wall crown, crown of a wall. Section between St. Jacob tower and the Drezvenik tower. So it's not on the tower. City walls walkway - this is Z13 - city walls walkway near the Drezvenik tower; it doesn't say it's on the tower. Z14, city wall walkway, section between Drezvenik tower and the tower of St. Katarina. So it's not on Drezvenik tower; it's on adjacent areas to the tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at Z12, 13, and 14, this damage that you found in A1 is not indicated, is it? Annex 3 of your report.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can please find in the preliminary report, P51, which comprises October, November, and December, can you please find this particular piece of damage, October and November, from your report. I can tell you straight up that it's not there, but please if you want to have a go yourself, you can just try to go through it yourself and see if you can find it. So if you can, please feel free to do so and have a go.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well normally this was -- we were asking them to look for damage from the 6th of December bombardment. I see that in preliminary report on the war-drove [sic] section, October, November, December 1991. Well, they've entitled it that. The damage that I picked up in the earlier -- the earlier bombardments is not in this and I am not too surprised that it's not in it, because -- with the instructions we had given was that it was for the 6th of December. Now, that didn't mean they wouldn't pick up some of that earlier damage, especially when it was right together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that all the damages sustained in the Old Town throughout those three months were assigned as damages inflicted on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not supposed to do that. They were supposed to find the damage that was the 6th of December and not from the earlier bombardments. I have seen one or two forms in which there is mention made of earlier damage, but it would be normal according to the assignment that this damage would not show up on these forms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, P51, the report, is it a report on the damage inflicted in October, November, and December, as its name seems to suggest, or not? Or is this a report on the 6th of December damage? If anyone, you should be in a position to know, since you claim to be the author of this report.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not claim to be the author of the report of the Institution for the Protection of Cultural Heritage in Dubrovnik. I can claim to be an important contributor to the methodology of that report. I have not studied this report in detail. I notice just flipping through that we have mainly 6th of December --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So Drezvenik, damage from October, this is something that we can't seem to find in the preliminary report marked as P51. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can't find this damage here, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next thing I would like you to do is look at item 6 of the annex to your report, annex 3 to your report, the Sponza Palace. Did you establish any damage to the Sponza Palace in October and November?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see the entry which indicates indeed damage to the wall of the Sponza Palace from the earlier shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now I would like to ask you to have a look --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for this exercise being so inconvenient, because there is a bulk of documents that I'm trying to deal with and it's enormous. However, I must point out the importance of this procedure and you will see for yourselves. The witness drew up a report; these are damages sustained in October and November. All these damages from October and November, with the exception of several of those, have been attributed to my client, as sustained in December. This exercise will probably prove to be quite lengthy and it will take some time; however, I hope that I will be able to show exactly this. And this is the only way I can go about this particular task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, can you please go back to the Sponza Palace, insula number 17, 17-5. 17-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, this in translation is page L0048618. That's towards the very end of the document, second-last page -- one of the last pages. I think 18 is the last one, so it's one of the last pages. 17-5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found that, Mr. Kaiser?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've almost found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report October and November, damage to the Sponza Palace. That's what it says. Isn't that correct, briefly?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in the report, preliminary report, of the institute it is stated that the only damage that the building actually sustained was inflicted on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. This describes damage done on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The damage described as relating to the 6th of December, what is the distinction from the damage potentially sustained in October and November and that from December? Are there any indications in this document, 17-5, that there had been any damage at all in October and November, because there is an assertion here, a clear assertion, being made that whatever damage was inflicted was inflicted on the 6th of December only. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's damage to the roof, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how could one distinguish between the damage from October and November and the damage from December when one looks at the preliminary report of the Dubrovnik institute? Can one draw any distinction at all between the damage sustained in October and November and that sustained in December by looking at the preliminary report of the Dubrovnik institute?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I have seen in examples used, this is -- this is almost entirely damage done on the 6th of December. If you wanted to distinguish between -- really, between damage done on the 6th of December and earlier, you would have to incorporate or at least put an annex, the annex 3 from my report, if you wanted to be able to distinguish clearly. But the examples you've given are just the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, what we have in your report, the damage inflicted in October and November was represented in this report as damaged that occurred in December. Doesn't that appear to be correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't think so. I think the examples you've given -- you won't find this damage which is in annex 3 from my report on Sponza; it's not here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain how this came about. And why is it I can't find it here if the report purports to be -- to refer to October, November, and December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, somebody has written on the title page that it's October, November, and December, and all the chaps running around doing the work seem to be looking only for damage that was done on the 6th of December mainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do they know, those chaps running around, which damage was inflicted on the 6th and which was earlier?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had the preliminary -- okay. I know, preliminary survey. There was an earlier survey which was done by their own institute, and that one they had. This particular document, which is in my report, would have been transmitted to them later. They could easily separate, even on the basis of the first damage report for October and November, they could separate the damage out. It's not to difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't they? They wrote everything down as if it happened on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The two examples you have shown me are 6th of December damage and they have nothing to do with the earlier damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on, please. Were you in Boskoviceva Street?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please find the damage that you yourself ascertained in Boskoviceva Street in October and November. Can you please find this damage in the preliminary report of the institute that comprises October, November, and December, if you can please. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can help me by indicating the number of the insula, that would be nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My idea was that it would be much easier for you to find your feet there. I thought you were more familiar with that than I was but, if not, obviously if not I can give you a hand.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at insula 6-9.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document is L0061069.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The preliminary report as it concerns October, November, and December, where can we find the damage that you refer to in annex 3 in your report as occurring in October and November?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about my report now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm talking about is the following: In your report it says that 18(a), the house at Boskoviceva Street number 1, was damaged in October or November. My question is: If you look at the preliminary report as it relates to October, November, and December, where can we find this particular bit of damage that you spoke about in annex 3 to your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. You'll have to let me just check the two different accounts. I'll make one remark and I'll go on in my perusal. It appears there is damage in this report of the 6th of December. It appears that there is damage on the facade that is in fact also found in my report. It appears this is from a heavy shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what that means is the damage that you established as having occurred in November was classified as having occurred on the 6th of December instead. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least some of that. I would have to go through the rest of it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your submission that in the preliminary report of the institute, the only damage that is actually listed there is the damage that occurred on the 6th of December. Is that what you're saying, sir?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is supposed to be 6th of December damage only. This looks like it's a mixture of old damage and identification of also some new damage. The elements are not separated out. The time of the damage is not separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, the dates when the damage occurred are not specified in the -- are not separately specified in the preliminary report of the institute. There is no distinction between the damage that occurred in the earlier months and the damage that occurred in December. Am I right in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen some entries where they also indicate November as well. In this case, they did not indicate earlier damage on this particular form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I was about to pick my learned friend up on that particular point. I can refer Your Honours to an example of such at L0048498 which is in the same bundle which we're currently considering. The damage to Zudioska 16, it is listed as having occurred on the 12th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was just about to say the same thing as my learned friend and colleague. That's quite correct and this is precisely what I'm talking about. Some of the indications are very clear and accurate as to the damage -- as to the date when the damage occurred, but most of them refer to cumulative damage that was sustained over the months of October, November, and December, but which was represented to only have occurred on the 6th of December. There are many, many instances of damage that actually occurred in October and November, but all of it is here represented as having occurred on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at insula 6, building number 10, also on Boskoviceva street in your report, sir. Boskoviceva Ulice Street number 3 in your report. In your report this is 18(b) and in the preliminary report of the institute, the reference is page L0061066. Can you please have a look, sir. You established damage at Boskoviceva Street in October and November, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now look at what the preliminary report of the institute claims. All of this damage is attributed, classified, as the 6th of December, even the earlier damage that you had yourself established?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it looks like the damage done to the balcony in the earlier period is, in fact, also attributed to the 6th of December. I note some roof damage from shrapnel which is not in my report, and that seems to be done the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at 18(b), Boskoviceva Street. What does it say in French there? What sort of damage was inflicted?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Corbeaux en pierre", this is the well-supported section underneath the balcony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you can also read it in French because this will be translated for everyone.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. "corbeaux en pierre appuyant le balcon en pierre du troisieme etage casses par eclats: cette structure doit d'urgence etre reparee parce que le balcon risque de tomber dans la rue."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters' note. Counsel is actually wrong in assuming that the English booth works in translating --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It appears not, Your Honours. I was convinced. Everything here is so bilingual. But that merely appears to be on the surface. The problem, Your Honour, is that we only have this document in French.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So will you please then translate this for us from French into English. 18(b)/3. My apologies. I was trying to make it easier for you. These things happen. What can I do. 18(b) Boskoviceva Street number 3.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stone supports for the balcony, the stone balcony on the third floor have been broken by fragments. This structure must urgently be repaired because the balcony risks falling into the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, 6-10, this report, doesn't it state: "Heavy damage to the balcony, to the south portion of the balcony, the balustrade broke down." Is that what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
