utterances.text: This is the object that is damaged but it seems to be additional damage. Balustrade is demolished. A previous damage --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only thing I'm asking you about is the following. Let's keep things simple. What you wrote as referring to November -- you wrote about November. This damage, was it registered as damage that occurred on the 6th of December, without wanting to go into even further detail and without wasting too much time. Is that how the damage was registered, as having occurred on the 6th of December. Please, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you now please look at 18(c) of your report, annex 3. Boskoviceva Street number 2. Can you please tell us what it says in the description.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the windows of the -- the glass of all the windows have been blown out and the frames of all the windows on the ground floor and on the first floor had been damaged by fragments coming from the shots on number 1. But the conclusion that the damage is minor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we now look at insula 6-5. L0061660. Is that what I'm talking about, Mr. Kaiser?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found the location. I'm reading it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course not each word will be identical but, roughly speaking, is it the same thing? I believe that you as someone who holds a Ph.D. can talk about this in a dozen different ways. But my basic question is: Is this fundamentally the same thing?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that it is because we're talking here about actual shrapnel damage on the stone. This is -- in their report it's shrapnel damage on the stone basically. And in my report I'm talking about an effective blast which would knock the windows out and would -- could damage the frames of the windows. They mention damage to stone lentils lintels chiselled stone, first floor windows, chiselled door transept and stone pin, et cetera, et cetera. And then they mention the partial displacement of the roof cover as well. And south wall of the dormer window shaken showing a longitudinal crack. It looks to me like it's different damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now tell me the damage that you established. Where can I find that in the preliminary report for October, November, and December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't seem to be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please now look at Boskoviceva Street number 4 under D, 18(d). Insula 6-6 L0061061. Can you please -- what it says at D in your report.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The window -- the glass of all the windows have been blown out and the frame of the window nearer to number 2 on the first floor has been damaged by shell fragments. Minor damage. But it should be noted that this house is abandoned in the last five or six years, and the interior is in the state of impressive decay because of squatters. That's what my report says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now look at the institute's report. What can you find there?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This looks like it's different damage. Substantial damage to the eastern part of the building facing Zudioska Street. Cause of a blast by a shell close by; that is the synagogue on that street. Cable wall structures damaged. Plasters damaged on second-floor ceiling. Two direct hits to the west front in Boskoviceva Street inflicted indirect damage to chiselled stone frames of second-floor windows on the west front of the building. These are direct hits and we're talking about -- in my report we're talking about the effect of blast. We're talking about different damage -- different damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking is: What is the distinction between the two? Can you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about windows that are blown out basically --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please just plain your description --

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... We're talking about windows that had been blown out according to my report. Now we're talking the damage -- this is on the west front. We're talking about substantial damage to the eastern part of the building. Gable wall structure, which is high wall structure. And two direct hits. I'm not talking about direct hits. It's different. It's very different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please say which side is your damage on. Has this been determined in your report, which side the damage occurred on?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has been -- it's effective blast damage. So it comes on the west wall and it probably comes from one of these other explosions on the other side of the street. We're talking about --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report can we find this piece of information, which side the building was actually damaged from, which side specifically, which would enable us to draw the kind of distinction that you're trying to make. Does your report actually specify this?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 4, right? Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It mentions blast effect on the windows, on the west wall. That's a different thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which side?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: West wall. West wall that is in Boskoviceva Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does this say? Impact on the west front. That's all right. Let's move on. Can you please look at the synagogue under number 19. What does it say about the damage sustained by the synagogue at Zudioska Street in annex 3 to your report.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The windows have been blown out on the side of Boskoviceva Street because of panels that were placed on the windows of the synagogue, it is impossible to determine the nature of the damage. But according to the architects of the Institute of Conservation Monuments, the synagogue was very damaged during the earthquake of 1979 and has never been repaired. Cracks were apparent in the interior, but it wasn't possible to determine if they were -- they were still open or whether that was the effect of the detonations. It's necessary after the bombardment of the 6th of December to examine more carefully the state of this important heritage because of the age of the establishment and the richness of the interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now what I would like you to clarify is the following: In your report in annex 3 you reference -- you refer to damage that occurred on the 6th of December. So what was supposed to be after the 6th of December? How does that come across in your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is question -- is a question of the cracks. And there was a certain amount of shaking in the town from detonations on the 6th of December. And so it's really a question of seeing if the cracks had widened, if there was more damage associated with this trembling of the town. I think that is what is intended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you is: In your report in reference to October and November, what does the indication mean, the date specifically, the 6th of December? That's my question to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought I answered it. It was a concern that after the 6th of December that it should be visited to see if there was any sort of secondary blast effect or any trembling effect to the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was it actually hit on the 6th of December? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember if it was hit or not on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe there was something else that should have been done in addition to merely visiting, if you didn't know if and how there was damage in the following period. What did you base your recommendations on as to what should or should not be done following the 6th of December if you knew nothing about that, or if it is your assertion today that you know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were worried -- and I was worried that there could be some additional damage that could be caused to buildings that were damaged in the earthquake of 1979. This is -- I don't know if it's the oldest synagogue in the Balkans, but it is one of the oldest synagogues in the Balkans and it's a very important building in its own rite. And it was obvious that normal -- that it should be double-checked simply to see if there was any secondary blast effect that came from the bombardment of the 6th of December. I did not see this building after the bombardment; I was too busy in the other part of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do I correctly understand, Dr. Kaiser, that as you understand the report it does not identify specifically damage caused on the 6th of December, even though at first sight that appears to be what it is saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is supposed to record damage -- identify damage on the 6th of December. And it would appear that there are a few entries that it doesn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the specific building, the synagogue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We don't have the -- I'm sorry, we don't have the synagogue building in front of us here on the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're going to have to adjourn now until tomorrow. I will make an observation to which I invite the attention of counsel. It is very obvious from the effective cross-examination of Mr. Petrovic that there are significant difficulties with the preliminary report and annex 3 to the earlier report of Dr. Kaiser. Mr. Petrovic may need to spend the time necessary, as he has done in the last hour or whatever it was of today, in going through item by item to identify deficiencies that he has identified. That is a time-consuming exercise for him, for the witness, for the Chamber. Is it possible by consultation between counsel for that process to be short-circuited and these deficiencies identified and scheduled by agreement? I just make that observation now and leave it to counsel to consider whether there is going to be a way in which what Mr. Petrovic is now in the process of doing can be reliably done in a much shorter and more efficient way. And we leave it to you to consider and perhaps discuss. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Tomorrow again, Dr. Kaiser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
